name: Do I need permits for interior remodeling in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do I need permits for interior remodeling in Los Angeles if I am not changing the outside of the house?
mainEntity.text: Do I need permits for interior remodeling in Los Angeles if I am not changing the outside of the house?

acceptedAnswer.text: Interior remodeling in Los Angeles often requires permits even when nothing changes on the outside of the home. Projects that involve structural changes, plumbing moves, electrical upgrades, HVAC work, or altering the layout commonly need review. Cosmetic-only work such as painting, trim replacement, or simple flooring often does not, but the exact requirement depends on scope and city rules. Homeowners in Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood should confirm requirements before demolition begins because unpermitted work can create inspection problems, delays, and resale issues. The safest approach is to have the contractor identify permit triggers during estimating, not after work starts. If a project includes wall removal, new circuits, recessed lighting, bath reconfiguration, or window changes, permitting should be expected.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permits are often required even when the exterior does not change if the project affects structure, plumbing, electrical, or mechanical systems. Wall removal, layout changes, and major kitchen or bathroom work commonly trigger permitting. Cosmetic updates like paint and flooring usually do not, but local rules can vary by city and scope.
